prompt: Some people think that children should start learning a foreign language at primary school, while others believe it is better to wait until secondary school. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
People have different views about when children should start learning a foreign language. While many individuals argue that youngsters should start in primary school, others believe they should wait until secondary school. In my opinion, learning a foreign language in primary school is the wiser choice.

Supporters of starting a new language in secondary school argue that this would lead to better results. Secondary school students are more motivated to attend language courses and stick to the determined plan without any distractions. For example, a student in high school is more likely to be consistent and not waste vital time, because he values the opportunities he will get if he masters a new foreign and global language. As a result, students who speak a foreign language besides their native one are more likely to earn supreme chances for the future.

However, I strongly believe that primary school children with a great background in a non native language are more likely to be successful in life. Primary school youngsters have extreme flexibility and higher chances to learn any foreign language, since they do not have big responsibilities of their own. For example, a primary school student has large amounts of free time, so he could spend much time attending non native language courses or studying at home through educational apps. Consequently, primary school youngsters who have effective and determined second language learning plans from their parents would get the greatest opportunities in the upcoming years.

In conclusion, although studying a foreign language in secondary school can increase the chances to be consistent, I believe primary school children should prioritize learning a non native language, as it leads to better prospects in the future.
